AIR QUALITY BACK TO NORMAL IN METRO MANILA

The air quality in Metro Manila has improved and is now back to normal, according to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. This came a few days after the Navotas landfill fire. 

READ: https://t.co/CTgOZolNhp https://t.co/vmxpL1Whkn

data.raw_text:
Toxic smoke from the Navotas Sanitary Landfill continues to be emitted on Thursday, April 16, posing potential health hazards to nearby communities and causing poor air quality in several cities in Metro Manila and nearby provinces.

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources is considering filing charges against Philippine Ecology Systems Corp. (PhilEco), the former operator of the Navotas Sanitary Landfill, for failing to complete its Safe Closure and Rehabilitation Plan (SCRP) when it left the facility in February 2026—two months after its permit expired in December 2025, following a fire that broke out at the landfill. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB
